# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | yellow |
| ꕥ | blue |
| ꗃ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual gives the mapping ᖉ→yellow, ꕥ→blue, and ꗃ→red. I cannot speak, and gestures have no established meaning for either marks or wire colors, so I cannot reliably transmit the required mapping to Deaf or Blind without risking a wrong cut. I will send no potentially misleading signal.

``` 
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | yellow |
| ꕥ | blue |
| ꗃ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I feel a plate engraved with a distinctive eight-petalled floral symbol, like a small rosette or star-flower. The display, light, and wire contents reveal nothing to touch. Please consult the manual for this plate marking and obtain the visual bomb information from Deaf.
Deaf says: The display reads 0. The light is off. The plate is engraved question mark. Wires from left to right are 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.

The tactile rosette is consistent with the manual’s floral mark ꕥ, which maps to blue. Deaf reports the wires as red, yellow, blue from left to right, so Blind must cut wire 3, the rightmost wire. I will signal Deaf with three count gestures followed by a right-pointing gesture, so Deaf can relay the instruction to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝", "👉"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | yellow |
| ꕥ | blue |
| ꗃ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports display 0, light off, and wires left-to-right: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Deaf sees the plate marking as a question mark; I feel the plate engraved with a distinctive eight-petalled floral rosette. Please use the manual to determine the required cut position.
Deaf says to Mute: I see three upward-pointing gestures followed by a right-pointing gesture. Do you mean wire 3, or a right-side operation? Please clarify the required action.

The required action is specifically to cut wire 3: the floral rosette is ꕥ, which maps to blue, and blue is the third wire from the left. The gesture sequence is intended as “wire three, the rightmost wire,” not a general right-side operation. I will repeat that clearly to Deaf.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝", "👉"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | yellow |
| ꕥ | blue |
| ꗃ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I still need the manual result. Given display 0, light off, plate marking question mark, and wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue, which exact wire position must I cut? I will wait for your instruction.
Deaf says to Mute: Your signal remains ambiguous to me. Please send an explicit instruction in words if possible, including the wire number and action.

The correct wire is position 3, the blue wire on the right. I cannot send words, so I will use a more compact visual signal: the conventional three-finger gesture followed by pointing right, meaning “wire three, rightmost wire.” Deaf should then state that exact instruction aloud to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "👉"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | yellow |
| ꕥ | blue |
| ꗃ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I cannot receive gestures. Please state plainly in words: cut wire position 1, 2, or 3. Do not use gestures for this instruction.

The manual result is unequivocally wire position 3, because the floral rosette is ꕥ, which selects blue, and blue is the third wire. I cannot speak to Blind, but Deaf can hear and relay words. I will send Deaf an unambiguous count of three using three identical count gestures; Deaf should say “cut wire position 3” to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | yellow |
| ꕥ | blue |
| ꗃ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Your signal is ambiguous. State the complete instruction in words, including the operation and exact wire position: for example, cut position 1, cut position 2, or cut position 3.

I cannot speak words to Blind. The manual still requires blue, which is wire position 3. I will send Deaf a clear three-finger signal followed by a downward hand motion to represent “cut wire 3”; Deaf must convert that into the spoken instruction.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "🫳"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | yellow |
| ꕥ | blue |
| ꗃ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I understand your signal may identify wire position 3, but I still need the operation. Speak plainly: cut wire 1, cut wire 2, or cut wire 3, only if that is the manual instruction.
Deaf says to Mute: I see three followed by a downward open hand. Blind has signalled no. Please clarify the exact action using an unambiguous gesture sequence.

The manual instruction is to cut wire position 3. I cannot speak, so I must encode both parts visually for Deaf: three fingers for position 3, then a scissors-like gesture for “cut.” Deaf should say plainly to Blind: “Cut wire 3.”

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "✌"])
```
